draft.title: Other readings of a text
card: Different readers can interpret the same text in different ways. Each reader brings their own focus, experiences and questions.

Readers often choose a focus. A reading focused on power looks at who controls others. One focused on gender looks at how men and women are shown. One focused on history looks at the time the text came from.
A reading is worth considering when the text supports it with evidence. Two readings can both be sound even if they differ.
Weighing other readings sharpens your own. You may find stronger evidence, answer a challenge or change your view.
draft.remember: Sound readings can differ. Weighing other readings tests and sharpens your own.

a.q: Two students read the same invented story about a headmaster and a new teacher. One writes about who holds authority, the other about the era's attitudes to women. What explains the difference?
opts: Each reader chose a different focus for their reading
One student has misread the story
Only one focus can be supported by the text
The story has no meaning of its own
a.why: Readers can choose different focuses, such as power or gender, and each can use evidence from the text. The misreading option is tempting, but a different focus is not an error.
a.clue: Think about what each reader chose to look at.

b.q: Leo reads an invented play as a story about family loyalty. A classmate argues it is about class power. What is the most useful thing for Leo to do?
opts: Test the power reading against the text and refine his view
Ignore it, since his reading was first
Drop his view, since the other reading is newer
Ask the teacher to pick one reading as the only correct one
b.why: Weighing another reading against the text can reveal stronger evidence or gaps in his view. Dropping his view is tempting, but a reading changes only if the evidence supports it, not because another exists.
b.clue: Which choice uses the other reading to improve his own?

a.best: Each reader chose a different focus for their reading

b.best: Test the power reading against the text and refine his view

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'a reading changes only if the evidence supports it', but the card uses softer language ('You may ... change your view'). Rephrase it without 'only', e.g. 'a reading should change because of evidence, not just because another reading exists.'
